:::{.custom-summary-block}
Claude Code is most useful when it handles the tedious parts of real work. This page shows how research and project-management staff at IPA apply it, the prompt patterns that matter most for that work, and how to have it learn your preferences over time.[^source]
:::

[^source]: Adapted from the [Claude Code guide for IPA Colombia](https://github.com/juanfegarIPA/claude-code-ipa-colombia) by Juan Felipe García Rodríguez and Diego Quintero Mogollón, used under the [MIT License](https://github.com/juanfegarIPA/claude-code-ipa-colombia/blob/main/LICENSE).

:::{.callout-tip appearance="simple"}

## Key Takeaways

- Claude Code earns its place on research and operations work: writing and running analysis code, drafting and structuring communications, and keeping project context in one place.
- Describe the outcome you want and let Claude do the tedious part; you keep control of the data and the decisions.
- Have Claude remember your corrections so it works closer to your style over time.

:::

### Have Claude Code run your Stata code

<!-- Fill (FLAGSHIP — Daniel: single most important use case): the write, run,
read loop. Claude Code does not just write a do-file; from the terminal it runs
Stata in batch mode, reads the resulting log, and debugs and iterates until the
code works. Walk it end to end with a generic example (a regression or a merge).
How it detects failure: Claude scans the .log for a Stata return code of the form
r(###) (for example r(111) variable not found, r(198) syntax error) — that code
means the run errored, so Claude fixes the do-file and re-runs. Show that cycle.
Terminal track (Stata command-line executable on PATH). Structure and code only,
